summary.short: Uruguay's free zones law (zonas francas; promulgation 17/12/1987 per document header) lets the Executive designate free zones run by the State or authorized developers, admits user companies under approved contracts, grants national tax and trade exemptions, and sets local-hiring and sanction rules.
summary.long: Ley 15.921 sets the regime for free zones (zonas francas) in Uruguay. Chapter I declares their promotion a national interest, lets the Executive determine zone areas, and allows expropriation for siting. Chapter II assigns administration and control to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Dirección Nacional de Zonas Francas, and provides for exploitation by the State or authorized private developers under paid authorization, with possible revocation. Chapter III governs users: contracts need prior approval and registration; authorizations run up to 15 years for industrial and 10 years for commercial or service activities, and 5 years for indirect users; users must employ at least 75% Uruguayan personnel (50% for services); teleworking is allowed under conditions; sworn declarations are due every two years. Chapter IV exempts users from national taxes on their activities, excludes social security contributions, exempts certain intellectual property income, and exempts imports and exports of goods; public utilities may set promotional tariffs. Chapters V and VI cover buildings, goods in zones, retail sales (generally prohibited, with exceptions) and free movement of securities. Chapter VII sets fines up to UI 10,000,000, prohibitions on operations, and loss of benefits. Chapter VIII allows thematic audiovisual and entertainment zones outside the Metropolitan Area, defined as 40 km from central Montevideo.

notes: Consolidated Uruguayan web version (Documento Actualizado) with no as-of date beyond its metadata; amendment and repeal notes are part of the fetched text and are coded as relations. The target_instrument_id field is empty where the target is not identified in the registry. Amending laws are not coded as separate instruments here. Naming varies: Dirección Nacional de Zonas Francas (art. 5) and Dirección de Zonas Francas (arts 13, 28, 30, 32, 37). Art. 22 repeats a phrase ('cualquier exoneración específica cualquiera'), apparently a typographical duplication. Art. 14 refers to 'Capítulos 1 y VIII', but Chapter I has general provisions only. Several articles are marked as repealed (arts 6, 7, 9, 11, 23, 31, 39, 40, 41) and their text is blank. Developers and users are categories, not named entities, so they are not listed. Thresholds, obligations and other sections are outside this request.
